body:
The suspicion of lossy conversion to float is correct.

The current `_default_formatter` of pandas\io\formats\style_render.py (approx line 1720) has the following:

```python
    elif is_integer(x):
        return f"{x:,.0f}" if thousands else f"{x:.0f}"
```
This is therefore a python f-string conversion doing the work. A fix would be to change to:
```python
    elif is_integer(x):
        return f"{x:,.0f}" if thousands else str(x)
```
The `str` function does not lose the precison.
(And an even better fix would be to correct the case for thousands separator without lossy precision - but this is much more complciated and a separate PR for that would be recommended)

> (And an even better fix would be to correct the case for thousands separator without lossy precision - but this is much more complciated and a separate PR for that would be recommended)

```py
In [18]: a = 1234567890123456789

In [19]: f"{a:,}"
Out[19]: '1,234,567,890,123,456,789'
```
Wouldn't this work?

issue.title: BUG: long int formatting with thousands separator

repository.name: pandas
repository.description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more

issue.body:
The previous PR #52686 for issue #52272 had three flaws:

- it did not account for long integer display with thousands separator.
- it added tests that had nothing to do with the fix that it employed.
- a test added was specific only to the latex output.

This PR reverts the tests, and adds a more generic test which is applied to all styler output modes by default.

**The previous whatsnew for 2.1.0 is sufficient to leave in place**.
